title: Free Will and Character
summary: Character as the self you build by the choices you automate. A later floor, not a substitute for volition.

lessons.title: The self you build
lessons.objective: Name character as the self you build, not a finished self you are handed.

exercises.prompt: On this floor, what is character?

choices.text: The self you build
A finished self issued at birth
A substitute for free will
A mood that discovers facts

feedback.note: Character names the self you build. It is not a package you are handed, and it does not stand in for volition.

exercises.prompt: Who builds that self?

choices.text: You, by the choices you make
A nature that writes the self for you
Other people, by their verdict
Chance, with no pattern of choice

feedback.note: The building is yours. Character is the self those choices make, not a script written without you.

exercises.prompt: Match each term to what this floor means by it.

feedback.note: Character is the self you build by choosing. A self simply issued to you is the claim this floor rejects.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit’s line for what character is.

feedback.note: The short form is: character is the self you build. Mood and excuse are not names for that self.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that names character.

feedback.note: You build the self. You do not inherit it as a finished item, and a mood is not the name of character.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, this is just how I am, so I never chose it. What does that miss?

choices.text: That character is a self you build
That character replaces volition
That feelings are tools of knowledge
That the body is at war with the mind

feedback.note: A standing way of being is still a self that was built. Saying you never chose it skips the building this floor is about.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast with a finished self.

parts.text: You are not handed a finished

feedback.note: Nothing on this floor issues a finished character. The self is something you build.

exercises.prompt: Match each description to its status on this floor.

feedback.note: Character names the self, and that self is shaped by choices. It is not finished before any choosing.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about how the self is made.

feedback.note: Choosing is how the self gets built. Inheriting a finished character, or taking a vote on one, is not this floor’s account.

lessons.title: Choices you automate
lessons.objective: Show that character is formed when choices are repeated until they run as a standing policy.

exercises.prompt: What does automate mean on this floor?

choices.text: A choice repeated until it runs as your standing policy
A machine that chooses in your place
Losing the power to choose
A one-time whim with no repeat

feedback.note: To automate a choice is to repeat it until it is the policy you usually follow. It is not a machine, and it is not the end of choosing.

exercises.prompt: Character takes shape when choices are what?

choices.text: Repeated until they become your usual way
Made once and then forgotten
Assigned by other people
Replaced by feelings

feedback.note: One forgotten choice does not yet make a character. The self is built by the choices you keep until they are usual.

exercises.prompt: Match each stage to what it is.

pairs.right: A start, not yet a character
The standing policy of the self

feedback.note: A single choice starts the work. Repetition automates it. The result is a standing policy, which is the self you have built.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line about how the self is built.

parts.text: You build the self by the choices you

feedback.note: The unit’s verb is automate. The choices that build character are the ones you repeat until they run as policy.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about automating choices.

feedback.note: Character is built by choices you automate. Feelings do not do that work, and automation does not erase the choice.

exercises.prompt: A policy now runs without a fresh debate every time. What has happened?

choices.text: The choice has been automated into character
Free will has been cancelled
The choice was never yours
Character arrived before any choice

feedback.note: Skipping a fresh debate means the choice has become standing policy. It does not mean the choice was never yours, or that will is gone.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line about an automated choice.

parts.text: An automated choice is one you no longer

feedback.note: Automation means the choice runs without a new debate from scratch. You did not inherit it, cancel it, or put it to a vote.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to its place in building character.

pairs.right: What that policy becomes part of

feedback.note: While you still debate the choice from scratch, it is not yet automated. A standing policy is the automated choice, and it becomes part of the self.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that defines automation here.

feedback.note: On this floor, automation means the choice runs as policy. A whim or an excuse is not that standing policy.

lessons.title: A later floor
lessons.objective: Place character after volition: a later floor, not the base of the ladder.

exercises.prompt: Where does character sit relative to volition?

choices.text: Later. Volition comes first.
Before any power to choose exists
In place of the basic axioms
As the start of the study of the senses

feedback.note: Character is a later floor. Volition is already in place before you study the self those choices build.

exercises.prompt: Why is character not the ground floor?

choices.text: It is built from choices, so the power to choose comes first
Because character cancels identity
Because feelings come before facts
Because the senses invent the self

feedback.note: You cannot build a self by choices unless choosing is already real. That is why this floor comes after volition.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to its place in the order.

pairs.right: Will first, then the self you build

feedback.note: Volition is earlier. Character is later. The order is will first, then the self you build by choosing.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line about where character sits.

feedback.note: Call it a later floor, not the base. It is not first, and it is not a substitute for the floor under it.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that places the two floors.

feedback.note: Character comes later than volition. It does not come before volition, and it is not studied instead of volition.

exercises.prompt: What goes wrong if you call character the base?

choices.text: You treat the result as if it came before the power to choose
You correctly replace free will
You make volition itself automatic
You put a code of virtues in place of facts

feedback.note: Character is a result of choices. Putting it at the base pretends the result arrived before the power that builds it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the order in one line.

parts.text: volition is already in place, not

feedback.note: Character comes after volition is in place. It does not come before that power, and it is not skipped or swapped in.

exercises.prompt: Match each role to the right floor.

feedback.note: Volition has to be in place already. Character sits later. Being the base is not its job.

exercises.prompt: Build the study order.

feedback.note: The ladder order is volition before character. Character is not studied first, and it is not studied instead of volition.

lessons.title: Not a substitute
lessons.objective: Show that an automated character does not stand in for the choice you still have.

exercises.prompt: Can character substitute for volition?

choices.text: No. It is built by choices and does not replace them.
Yes. Once a policy is automated, choice is over.
Yes. Character chooses in your place.
Only if other people agree that it does.

feedback.note: Character is not a substitute for volition. Automating a choice does not hand the choosing to a policy or to other people.

exercises.prompt: A standing policy still leaves you what?

choices.text: Able to choose, including to keep the policy or to change it
Unable to choose at all
Free of any further choice
Issued a new self with no choosing left

feedback.note: A policy can run without a fresh debate and still be yours to keep or to change. Automation is not the end of volition.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its role on this floor.

feedback.note: Volition is the power to choose. Character is what repeated choices make. A substitute is the relation this floor denies.

exercises.prompt: Complete the warning in the unit summary.

feedback.note: The summary says character is not a substitute for volition. It is not a cause that replaces choice, and it is not a percept.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states the limit.

feedback.note: Character is not a substitute for volition. A mood or a proof is not what stands in that sentence.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, my character made me do it, so I had no choice. What does this floor answer?

choices.text: Character is the self those choices built. It does not erase the choice.
Character is the primary choice to focus.
Emotions discover the facts for you.
The body chooses and the mind only watches.

feedback.note: A built self is not an excuse that cancels choice. Character records the choices you automated. It does not take their place.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line about a policy and the power to choose.

feedback.note: Automation does not erase the power to choose. The policy is not a sensation, and it is not settled by a vote.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to how this floor treats it.

pairs.left: It made me, so I had no choice
Built by the choices you automate
Still yours to keep or to change

feedback.note: Character is built by the choices you automate, and those choices stay yours to keep or to change. The no-choice excuse is rejected.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about choice after a policy is set.

feedback.note: You still choose after a policy is automated. The policy is not something you merely inherit, and choice is not gone.

lessons.title: Will, then character
lessons.objective: Hold the unit in one order: free will first, then the self those choices make automatic.

exercises.prompt: What is the order of this unit?

choices.text: Free will first, then the character those choices automate
Character first, then a will that follows it
Feelings first, then the facts
The body first, then a separate mind

feedback.note: Free will comes first. Character is the later self built when those choices are automated.

exercises.prompt: On this floor, free will is what?

choices.text: The power that the later floor of character does not replace
The same thing as a finished character
A passing mood
A social vote about who you are

feedback.note: Free will is the power to choose. Character comes later and does not replace that power, duplicate it, or put it to a vote.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the unit to its place.

feedback.note: Will comes first. You automate the choices you repeat. Character is the self that standing policy becomes.

exercises.prompt: Complete the order in the unit’s own words.

feedback.note: The order is free will first, and character as a later floor. A mood does not take will’s place, and character is not studied instead.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states the order.

feedback.note: Free will comes first and character comes later. Character does not come instead of will, and will is not dropped.

exercises.prompt: Which move mixes the two floors up?

choices.text: Treating character as a substitute for the choice that builds it
Saying you build the self by choices
Saying automation is a repeated choice
Saying volition stays in place

feedback.note: The mix-up is using character as a substitute for volition. Building, automating, and keeping volition in place are the unit’s own claims.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line that joins automation to the self.

feedback.note: The choices you automate become the self you have built. They do not cancel that self, and a percept is not the name for it.

exercises.prompt: Match each summary phrase to what it says.

feedback.note: Three claims travel together: character names the self you build, it sits on a later floor, and it is not a substitute for volition.

exercises.prompt: Build the closing line of the unit.

feedback.note: Automating choices is how you build the self. That work does not cancel volition, and volition is not one of the choices being named as the self.
